problem: L-ZSON asks an agent to find a target described in free-form language (e.g. 'cat-shaped mug') in an unseen environment with no map. Prior zero-shot baselines (CoW, OWL-CoW) pair a CLIP or OWL-ViT detector with uninformed frontier-based exploration. That exploration ignores scene semantics, and the detectors struggle to localize small or uniquely described objects.
motivation: Humans refer to objects with unconstrained language that falls outside detector class sets and simulator categories, and household robots must search without a known layout. LLMs carry commonsense priors about where objects co-occur (a mug is likelier near a table than a bed). The paper argues these priors can drive informed, mapless exploration, while an open-vocabulary grounding model handles the free-form target.
key_idea: At each step, rotate 360° and list the detected objects (YOLO) or caption the four directions (BLIP). A GPT-3 prompt then picks which object or direction to head toward, while GLIP grounds the free-form target description and triggers STOP once its confidence exceeds a threshold.
insight: On RoboTHOR, most of the gain over OWL-CoW comes from swapping in GLIP for grounding. GLIP-on-Wheels (FBE + GLIP), an ablation without LLM exploration, already reaches 33.2 SR / 20.3 SPL versus 27.5 / 17.2 for OWL-CoW, and LLM-guided exploration adds only +1.8 SR / +1.6 SPL (35.0 / 21.9). In the real-world two-room test with a hallway, however, LLM exploration nearly doubles success (54.2 vs 27.8 for GoW, 6.9 for random). This suggests small RoboTHOR scenes under-reward semantic exploration. Two other findings: object-list prompts beat BLIP-caption prompts (28.46 SR), because four cardinal directions limit the action space and cause back-and-forth loops; and prompt phrasing swings the valid-response rate (PSR 52.3–100) much more than task SR (28.1–33.8), with the 'reply with ONE word' instruction placed first hurting most. The GLIP threshold G_th matters a lot: 0.6 gives 13.8 SR, 0.85 gives 35.0, 0.95 gives 18.0.
method: Scene understanding via rotate-in-place: at each exploratory turn, the agent rotates 360° in steps of resolution r, collecting 360/r RGB and depth images. Depth feeds RTABMAP and ROS costmap_2d to build a 2D costmap.
Semantic extraction: the RGB views go either to YOLO, giving an object list O (smaller r), or to BLIP, giving captions C for the Front/Right/Behind/Left views (r = 90°).

LLM-guided exploration: a GPT-3 prompt (e.g. Robot-Prompt: 'You are controlling a home robot... Which object from {O} should the robot go towards? Reply with ONE object...') returns an object or direction. The agent reorients toward it; an invalid response triggers a random direction.

Motion: the agent picks a point on the costmap at exploratory distance e_d = 5 m (in RoboTHOR) in the facing direction and moves there with ROS move_base for obstacle avoidance. This is mapless with respect to semantic planning.

Target grounding: GLIP runs on every rotation image, prompted with the free-form target. When grounding confidence exceeds G_th (0.85, chosen by ablation) the agent STOPs facing the target; otherwise it continues for up to n_r = 5 exploratory turns.

Prompt study: seven prompt variants across three axes (point of view, information ordering, captions vs. object list), evaluated by SR and a new Prompt Success Rate (PSR = fraction of valid LLM responses).

setting.backbone: GPT-3 (frozen, via API) for exploration decisions + YOLO (object list) or BLIP (captions) + GLIP (target grounding), all pre-trained and frozen
setting.training_data: none (training-free); G_th threshold tuned empirically on the RoboTHOR validation set
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with 360° rotate-in-place at each exploratory turn
setting.action_space: LLM selects a detected object or one of 4 cardinal directions; agent reorients and moves to a costmap point at fixed exploratory distance (5 m) via ROS move_base; STOP triggered by GLIP confidence
setting.privileged: none for decision-making. Success is judged by the simulator GT as 'target visible in view during rotate-in-place', a looser criterion than a distance threshold. In real-world Phase 2, hand-specified common-object lists per room are passed to the LLM.

numbers.extra: L-ZSON setting (1800 val episodes, 15 scenes, 12 categories). Success = GT target in view when GLIP (G_th=0.85) fires during rotate-in-place. Budget n_r=5 exploratory turns of e_d=5 m. G_th selected on the same val set.
numbers.evidence: Table 'RoboTHOR Results: Observe the improvement in Success Rate (SR) and SPL on both our approaches over the current SOTAs, CoW and OWL.' (also G_th=0.85 row of G_th ablation table)

numbers.extra: Caption-based prompt with 4 cardinal directions (r=90°). Same success criterion, n_r=5, e_d=5 m, G_th=0.85.

numbers.extra: Real-world, 4 rooms (kitchen, living room, bedroom, office) plus hallway, 8 uniquely described targets. Two-phase: exit start room to hallway, then choose the correct room. Hand-specified common-object lists per room given to the LLM. Success = GLIP detects the target in the correct room.

numbers_note: Omitted from the entries above: (1) the prompt ablation table (SR / PSR per prompt, e.g. Robot-Prompt 33.8 / 71.1, BLIP-Prompt 29.2 / 100), which was run on 'a subset of the 500 best and worst performing episodes'; (2) the GoW (FBE + GLIP) ablation, which the paper presents as a baseline (33.2 / 20.3 in sim, 27.8 in the real world). The G_th ablation spans 13.8–35.0 SR. Per-class breakdowns for RoboTHOR and the real world appear only in figures. Real-world GLIP accuracy: 87.5% detection when present, 8.3% false positives when absent. Phase 2 failure rate: 20.8%.
results: On RoboTHOR L-ZSON (val, 1800 episodes), LGX (YOLO→LLM+GLIP) reaches 35.0 SR / 21.9 SPL. That beats OWL-CoW (27.5 / 17.2) by about 27% relative, CoW (15.2 / 9.7), and the paper's own GLIP-on-Wheels FBE ablation (33.2 / 20.3). The BLIP-caption variant is weaker (28.46 / 13.5). In real-world TurtleBot 2 experiments, LGX gets 54.2% success versus 27.8% for GoW and 6.9% for Random + GLIP.
limitations: Simulation gains over the FBE + GLIP ablation are small (+1.8 SR). Most improvement comes from GLIP, and the authors themselves suggest RoboTHOR's small scenes are a skewed testbed for semantic exploration.

Loose success criterion (target visible during rotate-in-place, judged by the simulator), G_th tuned on the evaluation set, and GPT-3 closed API. Results are therefore not directly comparable to standard RoboTHOR ObjectNav numbers.
The LLM gets no memory or history and can mis-associate targets (e.g. 'olive-colored jacket' → desk, 'Red Bull can' → desk). The real-world study is small and uses hand-specified room object lists.
